Evolution can explain the existence of junk DNA as a byproduct of genome dynamics and historical processes documented by comparative genomics [d5]. Within evolutionary theory, repetitive sequences once dismissed as functionless are now understood as records of duplication, transposition, and mutational decay over deep time, consistent with neutral and nearly neutral models of genome evolution [d2, d6]. Analyses of selfish genetic elements and multilevel selection further situate noncoding DNA within an evolutionary framework, even when its organism-level effects are minimal [d1, d3].
